funnel.intro: How many people reached each step in this period. Every number here is counted from your own records — nothing is estimated and nothing comes from anyone else's dashboard.

funnel.caveat: These are counts for the period, not one group of people followed forward. Somebody can appear in a later step without appearing in an earlier one — a customer who walked in, was recommended, or phoned. That is why each step also says how many of its people were in the step before.
funnel.definitionsIntro: One line per step, saying exactly what is counted and which part of the platform answers for it.
funnel.definition.visit: People who looked at the site in this period, counted once each however many pages they read. Automated traffic is left out. Somebody who tells you who they are later is counted as themselves, including the visits they made before you knew them.
funnel.definition.lead: Contacts created in this period — however they arrived: a form, a checkout, an import, or you typing them in. Two enquiries from the same address are one contact, not two.
funnel.definition.quote: People sent a quote in this period. Drafts are not counted: nobody has seen them yet.
funnel.definition.quoteAccepted: People who accepted a quote in this period, counted on the day they accepted.
funnel.definition.booking: People who made a booking in this period, counted when they booked rather than when the appointment falls. Cancellations still count here — they asked.
funnel.definition.cart: People who started a basket in this period. Baskets from visitors you cannot yet name are left out, because there is no way to tell one stranger's basket from another's.
funnel.definition.order: People who placed an order in this period, whether or not it has been paid for yet.
funnel.definition.invoice: People sent an invoice in this period. A draft invoice is a note to yourself, so it is not counted.
funnel.definition.paid: People whose invoice was paid in this period, counted on the day the money arrived rather than the day the invoice was written.
funnel.definition.refunded: People refunded in this period. Shown apart from the steps above, because a refund is what happens after a sale rather than a step towards one.
funnel.definition.firstTouch: Credit goes to the campaign that first brought somebody to the site, however many times they came back afterwards.
funnel.definition.lastTouch: Credit goes to the campaign that brought somebody back most recently before they acted. The two models disagree often, so a number is worth little without saying which one made it.

reports.intro: What the business earned, who it earned it from, and how each figure was arrived at. Every number is counted from your own invoices.
reports.empty: No money has arrived in this period.
reports.label.cohort: What new customers went on to spend
reports.definition.revenue: Money that arrived, by month. An invoice counts in the month it was paid rather than the month it was written, and anything refunded is taken back out. Currencies are never added together.
reports.definition.revenueBy: The same money, cut by what it was for. What each cut covers is listed below, because a cut that quietly leaves something out is worse than one you know the edges of.
reports.definition.cohort: Customers grouped by the month of their first payment, and what that group spent in the months since. Somebody on your list for two years who buys today is this month's new customer.
reports.definition.funnel: The same funnel the traffic pages show, asked of the analytics module rather than defined a second time here — two answers to “how many leads” is how a business ends up with two numbers and no way to choose.
reports.basis.invoiceHint: Each of these invoices was for one thing, so the figure is exactly what was paid, less anything refunded.
reports.basis.linesHint: One invoice can cover several of these, so the figure is the value of the items. Discounts, postage and tax sit on the invoice rather than on any item, so they are not spread across them — which means this will not add up to your revenue total, on purpose.
reports.definition.productCatalog: Items on orders whose invoice was paid in the period, by the product they were.
reports.definition.serviceBookings: Bookings whose invoice was paid in the period, by the service booked.
reports.definition.locationBookings: Bookings whose invoice was paid in the period, by where they took place. Shop orders are not included: an order records where it was sent, not where it was rung up, and guessing one from the other would give you a number that looks right and is not.
reports.unavailable: Nothing you have switched on can answer this one yet.
reports.savedIntro: A saved view keeps the question, never the answer — so opening one always shows today's figures rather than the day you saved it.
automations.field.audienceHint: Only people in this group may enter. Leave it as everyone if the rule is for anybody the trigger brings.
ads.notCountingYet: Impressions, viewable impressions and clicks are counted first-party. A per-thousand or per-click buy can be reconciled against what actually delivered.
ads.noCreatives: No artwork on this yet, so it has nothing to show.
ads.noSizesDeclared: Give the positions this runs in at least one size, then add the artwork.
ads.field.tagHtmlHint: Somebody else's script, so somebody else's tracking. It only runs if this position allows third-party tags and the visitor has consented. Review it like any other creative.
ads.field.providerHint: Must match an ads.txt line. This generates a Google Ad Manager tag; paste HTML for any other network.
ads.txt.title: ads.txt
ads.txt.intro: Authorized digital sellers, generated as /ads.txt and /app-ads.txt. A hand-edited file goes stale; this is the list crawlers fetch.
ads.txt.empty: No authorized sellers yet. Programmatic demand needs at least one line.
ads.consent.explanation: This advertisement is served by a third party. Allow it to load?
ads.field.imageHint: From your media library. Needed for an image ad.
ads.field.clickUrlHint: The advertiser's page. Visitors travel through your own signed link, so the click is counted.
ads.field.altTextHint: What the picture shows, for anyone who cannot see it.
ads.field.headline: Headline
subscriptions.title: Memberships
subscriptions.intro: Recurring offers and the people on them. A plan is the shape of the offer; the price comes from the product, so there is only ever one price to change.
subscriptions.noPlans: No plans yet. Write one below.
subscriptions.manualOnly: Every period raises an invoice you send. Automatic card renewals are coming with provider billing.
subscriptions.field.name: Plan name
subscriptions.field.trialHint: Nothing is billed until the trial ends. Leave at 0 for none.
subscriptions.field.setupFeeHint: Charged on the first invoice only, in minor units (500 = £5.00).
subscriptions.cancel.period_end: Keep access until the period they paid for ends
subscriptions.leaving: Leaving at the end of this period
subscriptions.enroll.title: Put someone on a plan
subscriptions.enroll.intro: Manual billing: this raises the first invoice, or starts a trial. They can cancel it themselves from the portal.
subscriptions.enroll.missing: You need at least one contact and one plan that is on sale.
subscriptions.portal.cancelIntro: Cancelling keeps access until the end of the period already paid for, unless the plan says otherwise.
subscriptions.portal.failed: That membership could not be cancelled. Try again, or contact us.
subscriptions.dunning.hint: Retries at those day offsets, access continues for the grace window, then the final action. Notices go to the contact on channels they already receive.
subscriptions.dunning.off: Do nothing extra — record the failure
subscriptions.dunning.on: Retry, keep access, then pause / cancel / downgrade
subscriptions.dunning.retriesHint: Days after the failure, comma-separated. 3, 7, 14 means three notices.
subscriptions.dunning.finalAction: If they still have not paid
subscriptions.dunning.noticeTitle: Your membership payment did not go through
subscriptions.dunning.noticeBody: We could not collect this period. Access continues for a short grace. Please pay the open invoice, or the membership will follow the plan's dunning policy.
entitlements.title: Access
entitlements.intro: What a person may use is computed from grants, not stored on the page. A membership, a pass, a one-time unlock, a loyalty tier or a decision you make here all grant the same kind of thing.
entitlements.noCatalogue: Nothing is defined yet. A membership creates a site-wide grant on its own; add a more specific one here if you need it.
entitlements.field.name: Name
entitlements.grantMissing: You need a contact and at least one entitlement.
paywalls.title: Paywalls
paywalls.intro: A page does not carry “members only”. A paywall selects it, and a grant answers for the person looking. Gated copy is never sent to the browser to be hidden later.
paywalls.empty: No paywalls yet. Add one below.
paywalls.field.name: Name
paywalls.field.selectorHint: A path without a leading slash, or * for every page.
paywalls.field.requiredHint: Entitlement ids, space-separated. Empty means any matching grant, including a site-wide membership.
paywalls.field.upsellHint: Optional CMS page id. The teaser button on the block still uses the href authored there.
paywalls.mode.soft: Soft — a preview, then the teaser
paywalls.seo.flexible_sampling: Flexible sampling — same free views for crawlers and humans
assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.intro: An optional chat assistant that answers on your website, in your name. It is off until you switch it on, it can only do what you allow, and it stops the moment it reaches the limit you set.
assistant.unavailable: The assistant's settings cannot be read right now.
assistant.notReady: The assistant is switched on but cannot answer yet. Check the model, the key and the spending limit below.
assistant.setupHint: Pick who answers and which model. Your key is never stored here: you name the environment variable that holds it, so it stays where your host keeps secrets.
assistant.field.enabled: Let the assistant answer website chats
assistant.field.enabledHint: Off means nothing changes. Visitors chat, and you reply yourself.
assistant.field.providerHint: Choose No assistant to switch it off entirely without losing these settings.
assistant.provider.openai: OpenAI, or anything that speaks its format
assistant.field.modelHint: Type the exact model name your provider publishes. Nothing is guessed for you, because a guess is something you would be billed for.
assistant.field.credentialRefHint: The name of the environment variable holding your key, not the key itself. Leave it blank for the usual name.
assistant.field.baseUrlHint: Only if you use a gateway or your host's own models. Leave blank for the provider's own address.
assistant.field.maxOutputTokensHint: In tokens. Shorter answers cost less and read better in a chat window.
assistant.credential.none: No provider is chosen, so no key is needed.
assistant.credential.missing: {name} is not set on this deployment, so the assistant cannot answer.
assistant.limitsHint: Every answer costs money. These are the ceilings, checked before each answer rather than added up afterwards.
assistant.unpriced: This model has no published price and you have not set one, so the assistant will not spend against your budget. Fill in the two prices below.
assistant.field.spendCapHint: In the smallest unit of your currency, so 2000 is {example}. Zero means it can never answer.
assistant.field.spendPeriodHint: The window the limit applies to.
assistant.field.repliesPerConversationHi: After this many, the conversation waits for a person.
assistant.field.repliesPerHourHint: Across the whole site. {used} so far this hour.
assistant.field.priceHint: In the smallest unit of your currency. Leave blank if the platform already knows this model's price.
assistant.scopes: What it is allowed to do
assistant.scopesHint: Everything here is off until you switch it on, and the list is the whole list. The assistant cannot reach anything that is not on it.
assistant.scope.unavailable: Needs a part of Freeholder you do not have switched on.
assistant.scopeHint.hand_to_a_person: Flags the conversation for you and marks it unread, so nobody is left talking to a machine that cannot help.
assistant.scopeHint.request_quote: Files a quote request against the visitor's own contact record. The assistant supplies what they asked for; it never supplies who they are.
assistant.turnsHint: Every answer and every refusal, with what it cost. This is where a quiet assistant explains itself.
assistant.knowledgeHint: Published pages, the catalog, opening hours and these notes are what the assistant may quote. A fact you switch off leaves the index.
assistant.knowledgeEmpty: No owner-written notes yet. Published pages and hours are still indexed.
assistant.field.knowledgeBodyHint: What a visitor would need to hear. Quote this, do not invent around it.
